newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch take delivery of politically correct bananas.
newsitem.headline: Dutch take delivery of politically correct bananas.

text.p: The Netherlands on Monday took official delivery of its first consignment of "politically correct" banana imports from Ghana and Ecuador.
The bananas have the brand name Oke and will carry the Max Havelaar seal of approval.

Max Havelaar, already known for marketing coffee and cocoa, adds its name to products from farmers' cooperatives and companies in developing countries which promote environmentally sustainable production and fair wages and working conditions.
The bananas were unloaded at Rotterdam port and ceremoniously presented to Dutch Trade Minister Anneke van Dok. They will compete with the giants in the market such as Chiquita, Fyffes and Del Monte.
They will be sold by Agrofair Ltd, a company set up by Ghanaian and Ecuadorean producers alongside fair trade group Solidaridad.

"These bananas will raise the profile of Max Havelaar, known for its coffee activities. The fair trade concept is working but it needs to be renewed and the arrival of these bananas marks such moment," Max Havelaar chairman Jos van Kemenade said.
The bananas are due to be in 600 supermarkets from Tuesday and Solidaridad, which worked to set the deal up, said it hoped to achieve a six percent market share in the first few weeks.
It said the Oke bananas would be competitively priced against other top class bananas and only slightly more expensive than other firm's lower price produce.

"This means the relatively high profit margin of the A-brands, which arose due to artificially created shortages, European regulations and limited competition on an oligopolistic market, will be used to double the income of the of local producers without raising the price in the shops," it said.
In a joint press release, Solidaridad and Max Havelaar said that if sales grew satisfactorily it would be possible to bring farmers from the Dominican Republic and Costa Rica into the programme.

But it criticised the European Union import licence scheme, accusing Brussels of more or less eliminating competition in the banana market. "The market for new-comers has been nailed shut in such a way as to eliminate rapid market innovation," it said.
"All eyes are now turned towards the legal action the United States, along with four Latin American producing countries, has insitgated at the WTO (World Trade Organization)."
Between 4,000 and 5,000 tonnes of bananas are due to be shipped to the Netherlands under the Ghana deal, on which the managing director of VREL is counting to stave off bankruptcy.
"If this fails, we're finished, kaputt," Hans van den Broek told Reuters last month, adding he lacked the funds to pay the 830 workers.
VREL has 600 acres of banana plantations at Akosombo on the shores of the Volta River (92 km northeast of accra).
